newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - U.S. bond volatility crushed after data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - U.S. bond volatility crushed after data.

text.p: Implied volatility for Treasury bond options sank in the aftermath of the March employment report.
"It got crushed, especially in May," said one bond floor broker.
May bond volatility was trading at 8.35 percent late in Friday's session, down from 9.45 on the opening and at Thursday's close. June fell to 8.80 percent from 9.20.
Traders in the debt market said the tame 175,000 gain in non-farm payrolls cast doubt on market direction in the short term.
"That was the worst thing we could have had, a neutral number," said a floor broker in Eurodollars. "Now no one knows what to do."
Volatility for June Eurodollar options shed 1.5 point to 7.0 percent.
Other quarterly options lost 0.5 point, with September estimated at 10.5 percent, December at 12.0 and March at 13.3. June 1998 dropped 0.7 point to 14.3 and September 1998 declined 0.6 to 15.5.
The short-dated mid-curves were hit hard, with June down 1.5 point to 15.0 percent and September down 1.0 to 15.3.

Traders noted that while interest rate futures remained under pressure throughout the session, with the June bond finishing down 20/32 at 107, stocks rallied back from opening losses. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended up 49 at 6,526, near the day's high.
Perhaps intimidated by the jittery tone in futures, options traders aggressively scouted strategies but often stopped short of committing, the Eurodollar broker said.

Activity in bond options was sporadically brisk, traders said, and several sizable transactions were executed. One U.S. investment firm purchased 10,000 far-out-of-the-money December 120 calls, possibly to enhance a portfolio of mortgage-backed securities, they said. The firm paid 10/64 and 11/64 for the options.
A second transaction involving way-out-of-the-money options was a futures trading firm's purchase of 4,000 June 112 calls for a premium of 5/64.
Another futures firm sold 7,000 May 109 calls at 7/64 and 8/64, while a Wall Street dealer firm paid 1-25/64 for 2,000 May 108 puts.
